speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they are painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Fixed Drug Eruption.

Given your recent initiation of captopril, the sudden onset of blisters on the forearm, and the specific mucosal pain (oral and genital) appearing shortly after, this clinical picture strongly points to a drug reaction rather than an infection like herpes or Stevens-Johnson syndrome, especially with the lack of fever or systemic toxicity. I am confident in this assessment based on the timing and distribution of your symptoms.
